Cautiously constructive, with financial-stability caveats from the FSR. The FOMC kept the target range at 5.25–5.50% and emphasized “further progress” toward 2% and a “better balance” of risks, but will wait for “greater confidence” on sustained disinflation before cutting. Implementation remains in the post-2008 corridor framework (IOER at 5.4%, ON RRP at 5.3%, standing repo at 5.5% minimum), and balance-sheet runoff continues with monthly caps ($25B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS).

FSR-aligned risk context that tempers the tone:
- Bank funding stress has eased (deposit outflows stabilized by Q4 2023; BTFP ended March 11, 2024), but interest rate and maturity risks remain.
- Vulnerabilities persist in CRE—especially offices—and related CMBS exposures; some non-agency securitization markets recovered in 2024 but underlying CRE fundamentals remain a drag.
- Treasury market liquidity can be tested under stress; higher long-term rates and fiscal-debt sustainability concerns could keep term premia and borrowing costs elevated.
- Nonbank intermediation and leverage buildup, plus growth in money market funds, point to ongoing funding-structure fragilities.
- External and market risks (foreign divestment from U.S. assets, geopolitics) remain two-sided risks to the outlook.

Bottom line: Progress on growth and disinflation supports a mildly positive read, but FSR-flagged vulnerabilities justify the Committee’s patient, data-dependent stance. We trim the previously positive tilt slightly to reflect these risks.
